rationale: T, H-1, SG-1 and FR-7 establish required braking execution as the phenomenon to characterise; the collision outcome and FR-7.1 also support its timeliness. However, P's declared scope additionally incorporates associated perception/planning/control states based on their relevance to deciding and executing braking. The requirements and architecture establish supporting mechanisms, but do not establish that broad internal-state inclusion as part of the phenomenon required by T.
determining_elements: The scope includes “the associated perception/planning/control state relevant to deciding and executing braking to avoid collision”; this is the determining overextension beyond braking necessity and execution.
“Whether braking maneuver execution is required and performed in time to avoid collision” is supported system behaviour and timing, not itself an overextension.
The specified road, speed, weather and pedestrian-crossing situation is directly supported by H-1.
